items.title: Tolliver interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2021
items.q: The interviewer mentions a reviewer's observation that Tolliver's style 'recalls Clifford Brown.' The interviewee does not mention Clifford Brown, nor does he confirm or deny a personal relationship, only discussing his work with Jackie McLean and Andrew Hill.

ctx.x: Yes I mean you know as you gain more knowledge of arranging, orchestration, you know, compositions, one comes to realize that one of the most important things is the weight of the instrument against another instrument. And if you, you know, after trial and error should be able to realize that, you know, if you give too much weight on a section it’s going to come out sounding not like what you thought you heard. You know, see the classical musicians from the 1500s on, including Beethoven and all of the greats,…

I do. I think that’s why Ellington kept his band together for so long, right? That is an interesting observation. I had a quote here about both your composing and your playing. It comes from one of those Jazz on CD books. And this particular reviewer made the observation that most of your compositions instead of complex chords, I think he’s referring to like bebop, “Charles favors basic motifs, four or five notes in an ostinato,” and then he continued, “it’s very much harder to play inventively over such a…

Well you know I wouldn’t be where I am today, you know, in this art form, had it not been for Jackie McLean. That’s what I’m talking about, that lucky break you know. And my first, my debut recording with him, as you know, Jackie was a dye-in-the-wool, you know, bebopper. But that was, I came in during that generational shift just as you know the freer forms were being used. I mean he was already, he had already done “Destination Out” and a couple of other things which portend that he, you know, he wasn’t just…
